correctness.rationale: Every codeword must have six distinct cyclic rotations; exact rotation testing gives 54 candidates. The admissibility-extension lemma checks both ordinary Hamming distance and all ordered splices for a candidate extension. Any feasible subset has a unique increasing-order prefix path, and feasibility is hereditary, proving completeness of the finite recursion. Two independent implementations, one integer-based and one literal-string-based, each enumerate 6731 feasible subsets with level counts (1,54,814,3042,2480,324,16), none of larger size. Both reproduce the exact sixteen optimizers, four symmetry orbits of size four, and uniform 8+7 pair-distance spectrum. Checks from extracted package paths have been run successfully. No inference about infinite lengths is asserted.

value.rationale: Levenshtein introduced joint Hamming-distance/error-correction and comma-free separation as a structural coding problem. The length-six binary instance is not an arbitrary slice: it measures the exact maximum message alphabet when frame recognition is required without bit errors and correction of one substituted bit is required at known framing. The solution supplies a complete sixteen-design equality classification and a common pairwise-distance distribution, not merely a negative example or numerical upper bound. The precise boundary between aligned error correction and error-resilient synchronization is disclosed.
